sentence: It pops when it gets to about one hundred eighty degrees Celsius. Its hard shell holds the steam in, until the pressure wins.
claim: A popcorn kernel pops at about 180 C, when steam pressure inside its hull ruptures it.
source_title: Virot and Ponomarenko, 'Popcorn: critical temperature, jump and sound', J. R. Soc. Interface 12, 20141247 (2015) (recalled, not opened; DOI from memory, corrected by the reviewer, also from memory)
note: FROM MEMORY, NOT OPENED (the builder recalled this; no source text was read this session); a person must open the source and check the number and the wording before posting. The DOI was not confirmed (the first guess 10.1098/rsif.2015.0174 returned 404); find the paper by title.

sentence: The pop is over in a few thousandths of a second.
claim: The pop (the hull's rupture and the foam's release) lasts a few milliseconds or less.
source_title: Virot and Ponomarenko, 'Popcorn: critical temperature, jump and sound', J. R. Soc. Interface 12, 20141247 (2015) (recalled, not opened; DOI from memory, corrected by the reviewer, also from memory)

sentence: When it pops, the hole races around the film at several meters a second.
claim: The hole in a bursting soap film opens at the Taylor-Culick speed, v = sqrt(2 gamma / (rho h)), about 7 m/s for a 1 micrometre film with surface tension 0.025 N/m.
source_title: Culick, 'Comments on a ruptured soap film', J. Appl. Phys. 31, 1128 (1960) (recalled, not opened)
note: DERIVATION (calc.py, run it); no outside source. Own calculation from the standard formula; film thickness (1 micrometre) and surface tension (0.025 N/m) are assumptions, stated in calc.py. The film says 'several meters a second'.

sentence: The whole bubble is gone in about a hundredth of a second. Here, that takes about eleven seconds.
claim: A bubble about as wide as an egg (5 cm across, R = 2.5 cm) pops in about 11 ms (pi R / v, the edge of the hole running half way round), about 11 s at 1,000x.
note: DERIVATION (calc.py, run it); no outside source. The hole's edge runs from the puncture to the far side: half a great circle, pi R. Assumes a 1 micrometre film.
